description: Louisiana-only rules checked against the Revised Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless a lower maximum is posted, Louisiana's general maximum on a highway that is not one of the higher statutory exceptions is
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:61(A) says no person shall operate a vehicle on any highway in excess of 55 mph unless a lower maximum is posted, except for the interstate, controlled-access, and divided-highway figures in that section.

questions.q: The maximum speed R.S. 32:61 sets on an interstate or controlled-access highway is
options: 55 mph unless a sign says otherwise
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:61(A)(1) says no person shall operate a vehicle on any interstate or controlled-access highway in excess of 70 mph.

questions.q: On a multi-lane divided Louisiana highway with partial or no control of access, the statutory maximum is
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:61(A)(2) sets 65 mph on a multi-lane divided highway which has partial or no control of access. A fully controlled-access highway uses the 70 mph interstate rule instead.

questions.q: A speed higher or lower than the R.S. 32:61 maximums, set by the department after an engineering and traffic investigation, is effective when
options: The parish publishes the ordinance, even if no sign is erected
Appropriate signs giving notice are erected
The change has been in the local newspaper for 30 days
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:63(A) says the declared maximum, when appropriate signs giving notice are erected, is effective at all times or at the specific times the department determines. This section does not create a statewide school-zone number.

questions.q: R.S. 32:64, the general speed law, requires a driver
options: To drive at the posted maximum whenever the road is dry
Not to exceed a reasonable and prudent speed or the maximums
To stay at least 10 mph under the posted limit in the rain
To use 55 mph on every interstate
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:64(A) forbids a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions and potential hazards, and in no event a speed in excess of the maximums established by the chapter or a department regulation.

questions.q: Louisiana's crime of operating a vehicle while impaired includes a blood alcohol concentration of
options: 0.02 percent or more for every driver
questions.explanation: R.S. 14:98(A)(1)(b) uses 0.08 percent or more by weight based on grams of alcohol per one hundred cubic centimeters of blood. Impairment by alcoholic beverages is a separate way to commit the crime.

questions.q: A first-time Class E learner's license may be issued at 15 but under 17. It authorizes driving while accompanied by
options: Any licensed driver age 18 or older
A parent who is at least 25
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:407 states that accompaniment rule for the Class E learner's license. The license must be maintained for at least 180 days, unless the driver reaches 17 first, before conversion to an intermediate license. A licensed parent, guardian, adult at least 21, or licensed sibling at least 18.

questions.q: An intermediate licensee under 17 may not drive between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by
options: A licensed parent or guardian, a licensed adult at least 21, or a licensed sibling at least 18
A passenger who is an immediate-family member, even if that passenger is unlicensed
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:407(A)(4) lists those accompanying drivers for the 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. restriction. Other immediate-family members may also be in the vehicle in addition to that licensed parent, sibling, or guardian.

questions.q: Unless accompanied by a licensed parent, guardian, or adult at least 21, an intermediate licensee from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. may not transport more than
options: Two non-family passengers of any age
questions.explanation: R.S. 32:407(A)(4) sets that one-passenger limit between 6:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. Fellow driver-education students may ride when a driver-education instructor accompanies the licensee. One passenger under 21 who is not an immediate-family member.

questions.q: In Louisiana, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Louisiana issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Louisiana car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Louisiana, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Louisiana requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Louisiana complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Louisiana requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Louisiana teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Louisiana requires at least 15 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Louisiana: 15 hours of the supervised driving at night.

questions.q: In Louisiana, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Louisiana, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Louisiana not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Louisiana restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Louisiana new drivers: off the road 11 p.m. to 5 a.m..

questions.q: In Louisiana, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Louisiana drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Louisiana car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Louisiana car knowledge test has 40 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Louisiana car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Louisiana car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Louisiana, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Louisiana sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Louisiana, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Louisiana brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Louisiana, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Louisiana?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Louisiana can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Louisiana rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Louisiana's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Louisiana: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Louisiana?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Louisiana, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Louisiana left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Louisiana's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Louisiana seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Louisiana?
questions.explanation: Louisiana requires a car seat or booster until 9 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Louisiana: car or booster seat until 9 years.

questions.q: What is Louisiana's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Louisiana requires at least $15,000 / $30,000 / $25,000.
